q: 1. For the locating a distant object visible from two transit stations, the method usually preferred to, is
options: angles and distance from transit stations
angle from one transit station and distance from the other
explain: For a distant, inaccessible object visible from two transit stations, the method of intersection (angles observed from both known stations) is generally preferred since distances to the object are unknown/inaccessible.

q: 2. The orthographical projection of a traverse leg upon the reference meridian is known as
explain: The projection of a traverse leg onto the north-south reference meridian (parallel to the meridian) is called its latitude.

q: 3. The distance between terminal points computed from a subsidiary traverse run between them, is generally known as
explain: When a subsidiary (auxiliary) traverse is run between two points to establish the distance between them, the computed distance is called the traverse base.

q: 4. The included angles of a theodolite traverse, are generally measured
explain: Included angles in a theodolite traverse are conventionally measured clockwise, starting the observation from the back (previous) station and swinging to the forward station.

q: 5. The latitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by
explain: Latitude (the north-south component) of a traverse leg = Length x cosine(reduced bearing), since latitude is the projection of the line onto the north-south axis.

q: 6. In a closed traverse, sum of south latitudes exceeds the sum of north latitudes and the sum of east departures exceeds the sum of west departures, then, the closing line will lie in
explain: The closing error (line needed to close the traverse) runs opposite to the net imbalance; since the traverse itself trends south and east, the closing line to bring it back runs north and west, i.e. lies in the north-west quadrant.

q: 7. Axis of altitude level is
options: parallel to the line of collimation
explain: The altitude level (attached to the telescope) has its axis parallel to the line of collimation of the telescope, so it can be used to check/set the line of sight horizontal even when the telescope's own bubble is out of adjustment.

q: 8. The most commonly used set of theodolite operations are
explain: The standard convention for taking a 'set' of theodolite observations is to start with the face-left position swinging right (clockwise), then observe face-right swinging left.

q: 9. When the first object is to be focused, the scale, is set to 0 deg 00'00" and then
options: the upper screw is fixed , lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, to tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, the object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient.
explain: The standard procedure to set an initial zero reading is: fix the upper clamp, release the lower clamp, roughly sight the object, then fix the lower clamp and use the lower tangent screw to bisect the object exactly.

q: 10. In precision theodolite traverse for roads and railways, the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For precision theodolite traverses used in road/railway alignment, the permissible angular error of closure is taken as 30 seconds multiplied by the square root of the number of stations (N).

q: 11. The projection of a traverse line on a line perpendicular to the meridian is known as
explain: As per the book's printed answer key, this projection (onto a line perpendicular to the meridian) is designated as the latitude of the line in this text, though standard convention typically calls this the departure - readers should verify against their copy.

q: 12. The process of turning the telescope about the vertical axis in horizontal plane is known as
explain: Rotating the telescope about the vertical axis in a horizontal plane (left or right) is called swinging the telescope.

q: 13. Traversing is generally done by
explain: A traverse survey can be carried out using a chain (chain traversing), a compass, a theodolite, or a plane table, depending on the accuracy required, so all methods are applicable.

q: 14. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of exterior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: Since interior and exterior angles at each vertex are supplementary and their total for all n vertices is 4 right angles more than the interior sum, the sum of exterior angles works out to (2n + 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 15. In locating the details of inaccessible objects visible at least from transit stations, the method used is
options: by angles and distances from the same station
by angle from one station and distance from the other station
by distances from two different stations
explain: Note: this answer-key entry appears mismatched with the adjacent question in the book. The standard method for locating inaccessible objects visible from two transit stations is by angles from both stations (intersection); please verify this entry visually against your copy.

q: 16. Right face and left reading are taken to
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: Taking readings on both faces (face left and face right) of the theodolite and averaging eliminates multiple instrumental errors together - collimation error, trunnion axis error, and other index errors - so all of the above apply.

q: 17. An angle measured clockwise from the proceeding survey line to the following survey line is called
explain: A deflection angle is measured from the prolongation of the preceding line to the following line, and when the direction is clockwise, it is a right deflection angle.

q: 18. Centering error of a theodolite produces an error
options: which does not vary with the direction or pointing
which varies with the direction of pointing and inversely with the length of sight
explain: A centering error causes an angular error that varies depending on the direction of pointing and is inversely proportional to the length of the sight - shorter sights are affected more severely.

q: 19. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
explain: The spire test is specifically used to check and adjust the horizontal (trunnion) axis of a theodolite, ensuring it is truly horizontal by sighting a high point from both faces.

q: 20. The angle between the prolongation of the preceding line and the forward line of a traverse is called
explain: As defined earlier (Q210), this angle between the prolongation of the preceding survey line and the following line is the deflection angle.

q: 21. After levelling of an instrument is done what is the next up?
explain: After the temporary adjustment of levelling the instrument is complete, the next step is to release all the clamping screws so that the instrument is free for sighting.

q: 22. Theodolite is an instrument used for measuring
explain: Theodolites are versatile instruments designed for precise angular measurements in both planes.

q: 23. A 20 cm theodolite means
options: diameter of the lower plate is 20 cm
diameter of the upper plate is 20 cm
total height of theodolite plate is 20 cm
explain: As per standard nomenclature, the measurement refers to the diameter of the lower graduated horizontal plate.

q: 24. The projection of a line on a plane perpendicular to meridian is known as
explain: Departure is the orthographic projection of a line onto the East-West axis (L sin θ), which is perpendicular to the meridian.

q: 25. The outer spindle attached to the lower plate in a transit theodolite known is
explain: The lower plate carries the main graduated scale and is attached to the outer spindle; hence it is called the scale plate.

q: 26. The telescope is said to be normal when the
options: bubble of the telescope is down and the face of the vertical circle is right
bubble of the telescope is up and the face of the vertical circle is left
bubble of the telescope is up and the face of the vertical circle is right
explain: Telescope Normal (or Face Left) is the standard position where the vertical circle is to the left of the observer and the bubble is on top.

q: 27. The process of bringing the vertical circle to the right of the observer is called
explain: Changing face is the operation of transiting the telescope and swinging it 180 degrees to switch from Face Left to Face Right (or vice versa).

q: 28. The error eliminated by taking mean of both face observations is
options: error due to eccentricity of verniers
error due to imperfect adjustment of levels
error due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to horizontal axis
explain: Taking the mean of Face Left and Face Right cancels out errors caused by the line of collimation not being perfectly perpendicular to the horizontal axis.

q: 29. The difference between the sum of the measured angles and the theoretical sum of the angles of a closed traverse is called the
explain: The error found by comparing the sum of observed angles with (2N ± 4) × 90° is the angular closing error.

q: 30. The difference between the two bearings of the last line as observed at the first and the last station of a traverse is known as
explain: If the computed bearing of the final line doesn't match its measured bearing, the difference is the closing error in bearing.

q: 31. A traverse consists of six side, then the sum of external angle must be
explain: The sum of exterior angles is (2N + 4) × 90°. For N=6, (12 + 4) × 90 = 16 × 90 = 1440°.

q: 32. The distance between terminal points computed from a subsidiary traverse run between them is known as
explain: A traverse base refers to the line connecting the start and end points of a traverse segment.

q: 33. Axis method of traverse correction is used when
options: the angles are measured very accurately
the lengths are measured very accurately
both (a) and (b) are not measured very accurately
explain: The Axis method is specialized for cases where angular precision far exceeds linear precision.

q: 34. Right face and left face reading are taken to
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: While it also helps with collimation (Q319), the provided answer specifically highlights the trunnion (horizontal) axis error.

q: 35. The theodolite is an instrument used for measuring very accurately
explain: A theodolite is the primary precision instrument used for accurately measuring both horizontal and vertical angles.

q: 36. When the latitudes and departures are so adjusted that the algebraic sum of the latitudes and departures are equal to zero, the operation is called
explain: This overall adjustment process, applied to both latitudes and departures to remove closing error, is known as balancing the traverse.

q: 37. The direct angles may have any value between
explain: Direct angles (measured directly in the field between two lines at a station, typically clockwise from the previous station) may range anywhere from 0 to 360 degrees.

q: 38. The distance between terminal points computed from known, as
explain: The distance between terminal points, once computed from known data, may be referred to by any of these equivalent terms - traverse leg, base, or traverse base - depending on context, so all of the above apply.

q: 39. To avoid large centering error with very short legs, observations are generally made
options: by using optical system for centering the theodolite
to a target fixed on theodolite tripod on which theodolite may be fitted easily
explain: To minimize centering errors on short traverse legs, any of these techniques may be applied together - sighting to chain pins, using optical centering systems, or using targets fixed on the tripod - so all of the above apply.

q: 40. When the first object is to be focused, the scale is set to 0 00'00 and then
options: the upper screw is fixed, lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, top tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient
explain: To focus on the first object with the scale set at zero, the lower (bottom) clamp screw is fixed and the upper screw is released to sight the object, then the upper tangent screw is used for fine adjustment.

q: 41. While rotating the theodolite in the horizontal plane, the bubble of the bubble tube takes the same position in its tube, it indicates
options: the line of collimation is perpendicular to vertical axis
explain: If the bubble remains centred (same position) throughout a full horizontal rotation of the theodolite, it indicates that the vertical (rotation) axis is truly vertical.

q: 42. Can the vertical axis coincide with any other axis in any position of telescope?
options: Yes, with the geometric centre of level head
Yes, with the axis of altitude levels
explain: The vertical axis is a fixed reference axis distinct from the trunnion axis and line of collimation, and it is not possible for it to coincide with any other axis in any telescope position.

q: 43. For a closed traverse the omitted measurements may be calculated
options: length or bearing of adjacent side
explain: For a closed traverse with one measurement omitted, computation can determine any missing quantity - length only, bearing only, or both length and bearing of an adjacent side - so all of the above are valid, depending on which data is missing.
